reason: Prior packed-B work on the inactive full512 path regressed, so it gives no evidence of a gain here. The active-path panel layout is still worth testing because it targets the requested B access pattern and preserves K order; packing cost must be included. `panel_packing` and `b_panel_layout` describe effectively the same layout, so test only one if their implementations match. FMOPA reordering and moving loop control have low correctness risk but uncertain throughput benefit; prior active-loop scheduling trials did not show repeatable gains. Prefetching is cheap to try, but the prior inactive-path prefetch regressed. A-slice padding has unproven cache benefit and adds traffic. A transpose affects fallback sizes, not the fixed n=512 timing. Transpose fusion repeats A reads across 16 panels, making its expected cost high.
